title: Sentence building: verb second, inversion, Satzklammer
intro: The conjugated verb is always in position 2 of a main clause — not necessarily the 2nd word.
If something other than the subject opens the sentence (time, place, a connector), subject and verb swap: inversion.
If the verb has two parts (haben/sein + Partizip II, or a modal + infinitive), the second part goes to the very end: the Satzklammer.
nicht negating the whole clause goes at the end, just before the final verb part.

exercises.explain: ich gehe — the verb still agrees with ich even though Heute opens the sentence.
wir arbeiten — inversion after the opening phrase, verb still in position 2.

exercises.prompt: Even after 'Morgen', the verb stays in position 2.
exercises.explain: Morgen habe ich — habe is still the 2nd sentence element.

answers: Heute Abend treffe ich einen Kollegen.
exercises.explain: Time phrase first, then the verb (position 2), then the subject: inversion.

exercises.explain: After an opening time phrase, verb and subject swap: gehe ich.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the correct word order?
exercises.explain: deshalb also triggers inversion: hat er.

exercises.prompt: sein + Partizip II for a movement verb.
exercises.sentence: Ich ___ gestern spät nach Hause gekommen.
exercises.explain: bin ... gekommen: the auxiliary sits in position 2, the participle at the end (Satzklammer).
habe ... gearbeitet forms the Satzklammer; everything else sits in the middle.

exercises.prompt: Match the sentence with what happens to the verb.
pairs: verb in position 2, right after the subject

exercises.explain: nicht goes right before the final verb part when negating the whole clause.

exercises.prompt: Holnap a vonattal megyek Bernbe a munka miatt.
answers: Ich fahre morgen wegen der Arbeit mit dem Zug nach Bern.
exercises.explain: TeKaMoLo order: temporal (morgen) → kausal (wegen der Arbeit) → modal (mit dem Zug) → lokal (nach Bern).
